quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in which direction?

options.text: Indicate no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit outside business and residential areas?

options.text: 15 mph.
25 mph.
35 mph.
45 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 mph.
questions.explanation: Outside business and residential areas, the default speed limit is 45 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road when parking uphill or downhill with no curb. This prevents your car from rolling toward the center of the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Where should you stop your car at a stop line?

options.text: Before the stop line
On top of the stop line
Past the stop line

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the stop line
questions.explanation: Stop lines are painted on the road to give pedestrians space in front of stopped cars. Always stop before the painted line.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how close should your car be to the curb?

options.text: Six inches
10 inches
14 inches
18 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 18 inches
questions.explanation: Park no more than 18 inches from the curb when parallel parking. Always choose a legal spot that other drivers can see easily.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: A loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system allows harmful fumes to enter the passenger compartment. Keep your exhaust system in good condition and fix any leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Reduce your following distance.
Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make any sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: Your wheels have left the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel tight, lift your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Once your speed drops, check traffic and safely return to the road. Jerking the wheel can cause you to lose control or cross into other lanes.

questions.question: An oncoming driver has not dimmed their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the bright lights. This lets you see enough of the road to stay safe until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always give the right of way to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not yet been washed away. Drive with extra care on wet roads.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC. The type of drink you have does not matter either.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat back and putting your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as other areas.
You must slow down in the cone zone.
Only slow down if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully in work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: To avoid sudden braking or turning, you should look ahead ____ seconds down the road.

options.text: One to three seconds
Five to seven seconds
10 to 15 seconds
20 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. This gives other drivers time to react safely to what you do.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering until the car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for a second train on the other track.
questions.explanation: With two tracks, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has curves and turns.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you to drive carefully when the road is wet, as it will be slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Firmly apply your brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: When driving down a long or steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors for speeding traffic behind you.
Assume all traffic is maintaining a consistent speed.
Watch over your shoulder for traffic behind you.
Hold down your brakes to control the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for speeding traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for vehicles approaching quickly. Vehicles often speed up going downhill. Watch for large trucks and buses that may be going too fast.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening around your vehicle. Watch the front, sides, and rear to spot problems early so you can change your speed or position if needed.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities who display a disability license plate or parking placard.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: To avoid glare from headlights of an oncoming car:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline on the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead again to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to drivers.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They are helpful when driving in new areas.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your body removes about how much alcohol per hour?

options.text: Three drinks per hour.
One drink per hour.
Two drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies process about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many factors: how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, how much you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren or air horn nearby but cannot see the vehicle, pull safely to the right and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: If you follow a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive above the speed limit.
Get closer to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings if following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Can be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down and pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones use orange signs with black lettering. Slow down and pay extra attention in work zones.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side of the road when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: When parallel parking, leave at least ____ between your car and the cars in front and behind you.

options.text: One foot
Two feet
Six inches
Five feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Two feet
questions.explanation: Leave at least two feet between your car and parked cars in front and behind you. Only park where your car can be clearly seen from both directions.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Cannot exit the freeway.
Can either continue through or exit from your current lane.
Can stay in your lane and continue through.
Must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane will leave the highway and not continue through the interchange. If you are in this lane, you can change lanes to go through, or you must exit the highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when visibility is poor or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: The rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: When skidding on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas and turn your wheel in the direction of the skid. If your car has anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight ahead instead.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The larger vehicle.
The vehicle on the left.
The vehicle on the left must yield to the one on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the one on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the one on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely, let others pass, then go when safe.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let others pass, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the safest thing to do before backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Walk to the back and check what is there before getting in.
Check your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio so others know you are backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back and check what is there before getting in.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always walk to the back first to check for children and objects before getting in and backing up.

questions.question: A yellow light is showing at an intersection and you have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before it turns red.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you to stop. If you have not entered the intersection, bring your vehicle to a safe stop. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: When is it okay to use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: You have a green light and want to turn left, but traffic coming toward you is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection instead.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with a green light and approaching traffic, you can enter the intersection to get ready to turn. Wait in the center of the intersection for the oncoming traffic to pass before making your left turn.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter the road, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you see pedestrians.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must always stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic already on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely. This is true for marked crosswalks, unmarked crosswalks, and any street crossing. Always yield to pedestrians for safety.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal road conditions. You can drive slower than the limit, but driving faster is illegal. Slow down in school zones, work zones, and bad weather. If conditions are unsafe, drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice, drivers with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers do unexpected things. Tell other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians what you are doing. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and horn when needed.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You:

options.text: Have done as much as you can.
Must stay until the police arrive.
Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
May go on your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note. Include your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pump the brakes firmly in an emergency stop. This stops your car quickly and lets you keep steering control.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep grade ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If parking near a fire hydrant, you must park at least ____ away.

options.text: 15 feet
10 feet
5 feet
1 foot

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
You may use this lane only to turn left.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is about to change to a red X.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A solid yellow X means the red X is coming next. Leave the lane immediately.
